text: Git branching is a core part of modern version control, helping teams work on code without stepping on each other’s toes. When you start a new task, you create a feature branch from the main working branch. This keeps your changes separate until they are ready. Once your work is complete, you open a pull request, which allows teammates to review the code before it is merged. Merging brings your branch back into the main branch, combining your changes with everyone else’s. This workflow makes collaboration safe and organized, ensuring that the project always stays stable.
